author: Joshua Fluke
description:
Apparently the ideal employee works harder, takes on more responsibility, negotiates less, accepts lower pay and stays grateful just to have a job.

A recruiter says a $200,000 employee was miserable while a $60,000 employee was grateful and “aligned.” Another executive tells workers they should be thankful to be employed, take on more responsibilities, work more hours, complain less and even offer to reduce their own salary when business gets slow.

Then a startup founder explains that some of their “best hires” didn’t negotiate at all — including one person who took a 30% pay cut and another who walked away from an offer paying $50,000 more.

Because apparently caring about salary means you aren’t committed enough to the mission.

In this video, we’re talking about salary negotiation, pay cuts, recruiters, CEOs, startup hiring, job offers, compensation, workplace culture and the increasingly common idea that employees should act like owners without actually receiving ownership.

title: CEOS WANT YOU TO WORK MORE FOR LESS!
